restrictions: Two-block ordinary collision of complete SHA-256 with steps 0..31 on every block (standard IV, FIPS 180-4 padding, common padding block).

Restriction to 32 steps of the 36-step attack of Li, Zhang, Li, Liu, Qian and Zhu (ePrint 2026/1120): message differences only in W5-W9, W13, W14, W21, W23; zero state difference after step 21; all used conditions at steps <= 23.

Priced under collision-frontier-v5 (C = 2224): one-time SAT starting solution 2^39.8, 2^52 first-block 32-step compressions, 2^57 tail candidates each charged <= 1/4 compression (incremental steps 14-21); total <= 2^55.17.
Success probability 0.6 at the stated expected work (independent per-candidate success, run to expected work).

heuristics.statement: As in the source analysis (ePrint 2026/1120, Sect. 3-4), a tail candidate built from a valid first block and a table entry satisfies the 57 uncontrolled conditions at steps >= 16 with probability 2^-57, independently across candidates, and a uniformly random first block passes the 15 first-block conditions with probability about 2^-15.
heuristics.scope: The 36-step SHA-256 characteristic of ePrint 2026/1120 Table 9/10, evaluated on 32 steps (all conditions lie at steps <= 23).
heuristics.extrapolation: The source measured the 2^-15 first-block rate over 2^40 random first blocks and confirmed the full attack with a real 36-step colliding pair; the 2^-57 tail rate is the source condition count.
heuristics.limitations: Conditions are treated as independent, as in the source; dependent conditions could shift the rate by small factors. A full-compression charge per tail candidate would give 57.0 instead of 55.2.
